observed.facings.png: Four facings at one shared scale. South is a short, wide wooden ladder top: two thick rails with carved caps, rope-lashed rungs and iron straps, and its bottom edge is cut off flat. North is the full ladder seen face-on, tall and wide. East is a much thinner ladder at a steep diagonal: the top is at the upper right and the foot at the lower left, about 65 degrees from horizontal. West is the same diagonal mirrored. The east and west ladders are visibly narrower across their width than north and south, and their rails look thinner.
observed.south.png: The tops of two carved, iron-banded rails with one lashed rung and part of a second. The sprite is cut off by a hard horizontal line about 70% of the way down, which reads as a ladder going down into the pit. The canvas is otherwise transparent.
observed.east.png: A slim wooden ladder lying diagonally in the lower-right part of the canvas. The top end is at about (330,145) and the foot at about (235,345), so it travels about 95 px horizontally and about 200 px vertically. The rungs are roughly perpendicular to the rails, so they slope gently up to the left and are close to horizontal on screen. There is rope lashing at the joints and a small soft grey drop-shadow to the lower right. The bottom rung end has a short overhang.
observed.north.png: The full kept ladder, face-on and upright: two rails with carved caps, about five lashed rungs, iron plates at the top and feet, painterly wood, a dark outline and a faint contact shadow.
observed.west.png: An exact mirror of east: the top is at the upper left and the foot at the lower right, with the same steep diagonal, near-horizontal rungs and a small drop-shadow.
observed.scale.png: A pit footprint outlined in black, with a dark floor and a lighter wall-face band, and a vanilla human head at the lower left. The north ladder sits at the top rim and reaches down into the pit. The south ladder pokes up at the bottom rim. The east and west ladders sit at the right and left rims as small steep diagonals: each top crosses the outline at the rim and each foot reaches only a little way into the dark floor, about the height of 1.5 human heads.
observed.wall_context.png: Same composition as scale.png. The ladder tops sit on the rim line and the feet go inward toward the pit centre and down the screen. On screen, each east or west ladder's long axis is a diagonal that is mostly vertical (about 65 degrees from horizontal), not a mostly horizontal span into the pit.
observed.variants_1.png: Close-ups against the wall bands. North sits on the rim line and runs down the wall face. East and west, against the vertical wall strips, each run diagonally from the rim outward and down, mirrored. Their rungs read as near-horizontal bars across slim rails. The pair forms a V/Λ shape, and each ladder still covers more north-south distance than east-west.

reply.subject: RM_LadderPortable
reply.image_seen: 1: four wooden ladder facings; 2: short frontal south view; 3: east diagonal rising right; 4: longer frontal north view; 5: west diagonal rising left; 6: ladders around a pit beside a human; 7: the same wall-context composition; 8: enlarged front and side wall placements.

concerns.evidence: In wall_context.png, the right-wall ladder's upper end rests at the outer east rim while its lower end extends left into the pit floor. The left-wall ladder mirrors this placement. Their horizontal displacement carries them across the wall band; their vertical screen displacement also represents descent into the pit. A steep screen diagonal does not establish a north-south world axis.

Both side ladders visibly cross their respective wall bands from rim to interior floor in wall_context.png and variants_1.png. East descends leftward and west descends rightward, addressing the owner's requirement that they run down the wall into the pit.

The east and west views show the ladder's broad rung surfaces compressed by the side perspective, while retaining paired wooden rails, repeated rungs and lashings. Their narrower silhouettes follow this foreshortening; the images do not establish a smaller physical ladder.
The isolated facings show solid wooden rails and rungs with lashings and fastener plates. There is no pipe, hose or open bore whose plane requires verification.

The card specifies zero ports, and the facings show no hose sockets, couplers or cord connectors. The visible plates and bindings are ladder construction details, consistent with that empty port list.

The supplied wall compositions show the intended placement, but no assembled in-game capture is identified. They cannot verify runtime draw-layer ordering against the wall. The module explicitly requires an assembled capture before acceptance; an in-game view of every rotation is missing.

request.prompt: A single portable wooden ladder in painterly vanilla RimWorld sprite style, realistic, clean dark outline, transparent background, 384x384 square frame, object centered with a small margin. The ladder is plain weathered mid-brown timber: two parallel side rails joined by evenly spaced round rungs (about seven), slightly worn, rope-free, with small flat wooden feet at the bottom of the rails. It is seen in strict side profile, so both rails overlap into one thick rail with the rungs showing as short stubs and the ladder's thin edge facing the viewer, leaning at a gentle angle against a wall that is not drawn. EAST VIEW: the ladder leans to the right. Its top end touches the right edge of the frame area, where it rests on the rim of an unseen pit wall, and its foot stands on the ground at the lower left of the top, the ladder slanting up and toward the right. The upper end is on the right and high, the foot is on the left and low. WEST VIEW: the exact mirror image of the east view, the ladder leaning to the left, top end high on the left resting at the rim, foot low on the right. Both views use the same wood, the same rung count and the same lighting from the upper left. Only the ladder is drawn, with no wall, pit, ground or shadow plane, so it can be overlaid on the game map.
